_meta.description: Pipeline configuration: LLM models, embedding models, and SSR parameters

paper_references.ssr_paper: Maier et al. - LLMs Reproduce Human Purchase Intent via SSR (2025)
paper_references.sample_size_paper: How Many Survey Respondents is an LLM Worth? (2025)

primary.rationale: Lite variant chosen to avoid thinking-mode latency issues in the deprecated google.generativeai SDK. Original paper validation was on gemini-2.0-flash (rho=92.4% correlation). 3.1-flash-lite is a different tier and has not been independently re-validated.

secondary.rationale: Highest KS similarity (0.88) in the paper; best for validation runs

generation_params.notes: Paper used T_LLM=0.5 as primary; T_LLM=1.5 showed minimal difference. n=2 samples per persona was sufficient for stability.

embedding.notes: Paper found text-embedding-3-large produced virtually identical results. Small model is cheaper and sufficient.

notes.epsilon: Controls minimum-probability floor. 0.0 means one Likert rating always gets p=0 per set. Paper used 0.0 but flags it as tunable.
notes.temperature: Controls pmf sharpness. T=1 is the paper's default. Lower T = peakier distributions. Paper shows optimization potential around T=1.
notes.aggregation: Average pmfs across all reference sets per respondent. Paper found this more robust than using any single best set.

effective_sample_size_notes.source: Hidden population size estimates from sample size paper, alpha=0.05
effective_sample_size_notes.warning: These are domain-specific. Do not assume your domain matches. Generate more respondents than the effective size to ensure distributional stability.

demographic_axes.notes: Paper found age and income effects reproduced well by LLMs. Gender, region, ethnicity were inconsistently captured. Flag poorly-replicated axes as lower-confidence in reports.
